client.description: The name the calling program gave; diagnostic only, never an identity.

beforeId.description: Only rows older than this row id (the `nextBeforeId` of the previous page).

callerKind.description: Only rows of calls this kind of caller made.

nextBeforeId.description: Pass as `beforeId` to read the next, older page; absent on the last page.

AuthorizeKeyParams.description: A controller's Connections public key (`ssh-ed25519 <key> [comment]`) for this device to accept.

added.description: False when the key was already authorized.

canonical.description: The line is exactly the one Silo writes now (`restrict`, the bridge with `--key` and the key's fingerprint).

fingerprint.description: `SHA256:...`, as `ssh-keygen -l` prints it; absent when the key is not base64.

identified.description: The forced command passes the bridge this line's own key fingerprint, so a request through it can revoke that key.

BackupState.description:

the API's remembered destination field added for a client-owned folder picker.

idleSeconds.description: How long after the base capture the fork is left idle before it is captured again.

source.description: The checkpoint the idle fork came from; defaults to the source recorded with its base.

role.description: `base` records the fork-time state; `latest` (the default) records the current one.

source.description:
For a `base` capture: the checkpoint (or computer) the fork was made from. The
no-op baseline is cached under it.

baseline.description: Subtract the cached no-op baseline when there is one (default true).

maxLines.description: Cut the readable text to this many lines.

refresh.description: Capture the computer now (default true); false compares the last capture.

choices.description:
The answer for each item both sides changed, by item id (the `id` of a conflict, or
of an entry in `changes.diff`). A repository takes `branch` or `main`; every other
item takes `fork` or `main`. An id that is not in the reviewed diff, or an answer the
item does not allow, fails the keep and names the item. Databases take no answer.
Choices are checked against the reviewed diff and are not part of the review digest.

dataOk.description: Carry database changes even though no migration step covers them.

deviceId.description: The device that owns this; absent or `local` is this device.

dryRun.description: Check and report what a keep would do, changing nothing.

forkId.description: The fork whose changes are kept.

reviewDigest.description:
The `reviewDigest` of the `changes.diff` the user reviewed; the keep refuses when the
fork's changes no longer match it.

skip.description:
Item ids not to bring over even though they do not conflict. The same as answering
`main`; the report calls them `skipped`.

targetId.description: The computer to keep into; defaults to the one the fork was made from.

ChangesKeepResult.description:
The final result of `changes.keep`. `status` is `kept`, `dry-run` or `refused`; a
refused keep did not change the target. A keep that needs answers is `refused` with the
reason `choices-needed`.

deviceId.description: The device that owns this; absent or `local` is this device.

dryRun.description: Check and report what a promote would do, changing nothing.

targetId.description: The computer it replaces; defaults to the one the fork was made from.

ChangesPromoteResult.description:
The final result of `changes.promote`. `status` is `promoted`, `dry-run` or `refused`; a
refused promote changed nothing.

ChangesRequestParams.description:
Ask for a fork to be reviewed without keeping it: `changes.request` stores a
[`FoldRequest`] and changes nothing else.

counts.description: The bucket counts of the diff the request was made from.

deviceId.description: The device that owns this; absent or `local` is this device.

reviewDigest.description: The `reviewDigest` of the `changes.diff` the request was made from.

summary.description: A short text for the reviewer, usually the readable diff.

targetId.description: The computer it would be kept into; defaults to the one the fork was made from.

choices.description: The answer for each item both sides changed, by item id; see `changes.keep`.

dataOk.description: Carry database changes even though no migration step covers them.

deviceId.description: The device that owns this; absent or `local` is this device.

keep.description: The recipe's `keep:` steps to run around the keep.

skip.description: Item ids not to bring over even though they do not conflict; see `changes.keep`.

ChangesRequestsKeepResult.description:
The result of `changes.requests.keep`: the keep's own result and the request after it.
A refused keep leaves the request open.

allDevices.description:
Also list the requests of every connected device. Each row says which device it
belongs to; a device that cannot be reached is reported in `unreachable`.

deviceId.description: The device whose requests are listed; absent or `local` is this device.

unreachable.description: Devices a list across devices could not read.

ChangesRequestsMarkKeptParams.description:
Closes the open requests for a fork and target that were kept outside the engine: a
folder fork folded into its folder by the CLI.

deviceId.description: The device that owns this; absent or `local` is this device.

keepId.description: What `undo` goes back to, such as the folder's backup ref.

target.description: The request's target, `folder:<path>` for a folder fork.

sshAlias.description: The SSH alias that reaches the fork, when one is set up.

started.description: Whether this call started the fork.

state.description: The state after the call: `running` unless the fork could not be started.

urls.description: The URLs the fork's published ports answer on.

ChangesRequestsShowResult.description: A request, a fresh diff of its fork and the credentials the fork used.

counts.description: The number of changes in each bucket of `diff`.

diff.description: The `silo diff --json` document; `null` for a folder fork.

fresh.description:
Whether the fork was looked at now (`true`) or the last look was used (the fork
is stopped).

reviewDigest.description: The digest of the fork's changes now.

stale.description:
`true` when the fork's changes differ from the ones the request was made from; a
keep of the request refuses. `None` when this cannot be told (a folder fork).

text.description: The readable form of `diff`, or the request's own summary for a folder fork.

dropped.description: The name of the fork that was dropped.

ChangesRole.description: Which stored manifest a capture replaces.

oneOf.description: The computer as it was when it was forked, before any agent work.
The most recent look at the computer.

deviceId.description: The device that owns this; absent or `local` is this device.

ChangesUndoResult.description: The final result of `changes.undo`. `status` is `undone` or `nothing-to-undo`.

changedSince.description: What changed on the computer after the keep; the undo discards it.

main.description: `running` or `stopped`: main as the undo left it.

notes.description: What the undo could not do, such as starting main.

resumedFrom.description: `memory` when main resumed from the checkpoint's memory, else `stopped`.

Checkpoint.description: The common checkpoint view returned by Linux and macOS computers.

keepNewest.description:

quiet.description: What to quiet in the fork before it runs anything.

The content hash of the recipe this fork was built from. The fork's idle baseline

secrets.description:
Names of Silo-managed secrets the fork may use. The special name `github` copies

ClientMetadata.description: Client information is diagnostic metadata, not an authorization identity.

ClipboardContent.description:
The specification does not yet fix the exact fields of all clipboard
payloads. This tagged union keeps text and PNG bytes explicit.

ports.description: Its ports published on this device.

allRepositoriesWrite.description: With `allRepositories`: whether it may push to them.

agents.description:
Agents to install during the new computer's first boot, after its setup. A failed
install does not fail the creation: the creation job reports it and the agent
lists as `missing`. Empty installs none. A macOS computer does not accept agents
at creation yet (see the `macos` kind); `agents.install` installs one in a running
computer of either kind. An agent that lists as `ready` is the computer's own
report, and a computer can claim it.

networkPolicy.description: The new computer's network policy. Absent, it is open.

agents.description:
Not accepted yet: a macOS computer refuses a non-empty list, because its setup ends
with the computer stopped. Create the computer, start it, then install an agent
with `agents.install`. An agent that lists as `ready` is the computer's own report,
and a computer can claim it.

networkPolicy.description: The new computer's network policy. Absent, it is open.

recipe.description: Absent for a computer that was not built from a recipe.

computers.description: The computers the caller may see: all of them for the owner, the caller and the computers it made otherwise.

name.description:

A path on this machine: where a received file is written (it must not exist) or

resolvedAt.description: When the request was kept or thrown away.

reviewDigest.description: The digest of the changes the requester reviewed; empty when none was given.

target.description: The computer the fork would be kept into.

GuestClientStatus.description: Whether a computer has Silo's tools, and where they answer.

components.description: What Silo keeps in the computer and how each piece fared at its last reconcile.

enabledAt.description: When the tools were turned on.

endpointPath.description: Where the computer finds the address and its token.

host.description: The host name the computer reaches the channel by.

When the computer's network lets it reach the channel: now, at its next start, or
after a restart.

port.description: The channel's port on the device's loopback.

The channel had to move to a new port while the computer's network still names the
old one, which another program holds. The tools are not served, and no token is
written, until the computer restarts.

written.description:
Whether the endpoint file was written into the computer by this call. A computer
that is not running gets it when it next starts.

GuestComponentState.description: How one piece Silo keeps in a computer ended its last reconcile.

oneOf.description: In place and current.
The step failed; the detail says why.
This build of Silo cannot provide the piece.
Waiting for something else, such as an agent that is not installed yet.
Taken out on purpose because the tools were turned off.

A piece Silo puts into a computer and keeps current, with the result of its last reconcile
(at every start of the computer, and when the tools are turned on or off).

detail.description: Why it failed or is waiting, in words for a person.

id.description:
`silo` (the program at `/usr/local/bin/silo`) or `silo-mcp` (its registration as an
MCP server in Claude Code and Codex).

HandshakeParams.description:
`engine.handshake` parameters. `sshKey` is used by the Connections bridge
to install the restricted key; local engine clients omit it. `proof` answers the channel's
[`ChannelChallenge`] on the channel inside a computer, and is required there (lowercase hex of
[`channel_proof`]); `engine.sock` ignores it.

HandshakeResult.description:
Result of protocol negotiation. `clientId` is supplied on `engine.sock`
and omitted when the handshake runs through the remote control socket.

IncompatibleVersionDiagnostics.description: Engine and client versions reported when handshake protocol negotiation fails.

JobFinished.description:
One terminal job event. `result` remains the untagged final JSON value
returned by the method that started the job. The schema's
`x-silo-job-results` catalogue maps methods to their terminal result schemas.

outcomeChunked.description: The complete outcome is retained and available through `operations.job.get` chunks.

JobId.description: Opaque id in setup:, transfer:, push:, exports:, inspect:, or decimal job: space

outcomeChunk.description:
Present when the retained outcome is too large for one response. `data`
is an exact UTF-8 slice of the persisted JobOutcome JSON.

JobProgress.description:
The values emitted as the `data` field of `operations.job.progress`.

Payload member names mirror their source serde structs. The macOS contract
uses `computerId` as stated in 05 §4.2 E; the current MacosComputer row uses
`id`, a source/spec discrepancy recorded in the implementation report.

JobTerminalResultsSchema.description:
Terminal job values remain untagged on the wire. This catalogue roots every
method-specific result schema and maps the defined job completion shapes.

KeepAnswer.description: How an item both sides changed is settled.

oneOf.description: The fork's version is written over main's.
The item stays as main has it.

A repository only: the fork's commits arrive as a branch named `silo/<fork name>` and
nothing is merged or checked out.

allowed.description: The answers that settle it; empty when none does.

forkChange.description: What changed in the fork, in a few words.

id.description:
The id of the item, the key of its answer in `choices`; empty when no answer
settles the conflict (credentials).

mainChange.description: What changed on main, in a few words.

migrate.description: Commands run once the code and files are in place (database migrations).

restart.description: Services restarted after the changes are applied.

outcome.description:
`brought-over`, `left-as-main` (answered `main`), `branch` (a repository's commits
left as a branch), `skipped` (listed in `skip`), `already-there` (main already holds
it) or `not-combined` (a database).

reason.description:
`choices-needed` (both sides changed items that have no answer yet: `conflicts` lists
them with the answers each allows), `database`, `credentials`, `changed` or
`main-changed`. Older engines also said `divergent` and `git`.

checkpoint.description: The before-keep checkpoint of the target.

fastForward.description:
Whether main was unchanged since the fork was made, so nothing could conflict.
Absent when the keep stopped before main was looked at.

items.description: What was done with each item, by id. Empty when the keep was refused.

reviewDigest.description: The digest of the fork's changes the keep acted on.

`app/SiloUI/src-tauri/engine/src/runtime.rs::LifecycleStep` (line 1275).

boots.description: How many times the engine has booted the computer.

note.description:
Informational only: something to know that is not a problem and needs no action (for
example, an imported computer has no SecureToken). Never a failure detail.

deviceId.description:
The device that owns the computer. Absent or this engine's own device resizes here;
another device forwards the resize to its owner.

MacosJobProgress.description: The macOS progress projection from 05 §4.2 E (`MacosComputer` row fields).

MacosResourceConfiguration.description: Optimistic state check for a stopped macOS computer's resource edit.

MemoryPressure.description: The system's own reading of memory pressure.

NativeDisplayMessage.description:
JSON messages used by the native display stream. Pixel data itself is
transferred out of band through the shared-memory path.

NetworkPolicy.description: A computer's network policy, as the owner sets it.

hosts.description:
Host patterns: `example.com` or `*.example.com` (which also covers
`example.com`). Lowercase names only; no ports, no addresses. Used in allowlist mode.

presets.description:
Named host lists kept by the engine (`network.policy.get` lists them). Used in
allowlist mode.

NetworkPolicyHost.description: One host a computer in allowlist mode may reach, and why.

ports.description: The TCP ports allowed to it.

NetworkPolicyMode.description: How much of the network a computer may reach.

oneOf.description: Any public address, as every computer had before policies existed.
Only the hosts on its list, the hosts of its presets and the hosts its grants need.
No outbound traffic, not even name lookups.

acceptPresets.description:
When true, re-pins presets to their latest versions, accepting pending updates.
A normal save preserves existing pins.

expected.description:
The policy the caller judged the change against. When it is given and the computer's
policy is now another, nothing is saved. The engine fills it in for a computer's
agent narrowing its own network, so a narrowing cannot undo a change the owner made
meanwhile.

allowedHosts.description:
Every host the computer may reach in allowlist mode, including those added for its
GitHub access and its secrets. Empty in the other modes.

notices.description:
Things to tell the owner about this policy, in plain words: a secret wildcard that is
not added to the list, or a policy that could not be read.

presetUpdates.description: Presets of the policy that have an update to accept.

NetworkPolicyTiming.description: When a saved policy is in force.

oneOf.description: The computer runs with it now.
The computer is stopped; it starts with this policy.
The computer is running with its previous rules and keeps them until it restarts.

NetworkPreset.description: A named host list the engine keeps.

NetworkPresetUpdate.description:
A preset whose list in this Silo has hosts the computer's policy was not approved with.
The computer keeps its approved list until the owner sets the policy again with the
same presets.

addedHosts.description: The hosts the update would add.

oneOf.description: A computer's agent asks for something only the owner can allow.

key.description: Only the notice with this key is gone; without it, every notice of the computer.

and its camelCase serde names.

and adds the retained completed-job discovery list required by 95 §3.

OwnKeyResult.description: This device's own Connections public key, created when it had none.

buckets.description: Changed paths by bucket, when cheaply known.

requestId.description: The open review request for this fork, if there is one.

optionality match `runtime/checkpoints.rs` and `macos_computers/checkpoints.rs`.

archive.description: The name the old main has afterwards.

checkpoint.description: The before-promote checkpoint of the old main.

ProtocolRange.description: The inclusive protocol range a client supports.

PushOperation.description:
Mirrors the push-operation value recorded by
`app/SiloUI/src-tauri/engine/src/host_push_operations.rs`.

QuietSpec.description: Things a fork turns off on its first boot, beyond the scheduled jobs it always turns off.

scrub.description: Absolute guest paths (globs allowed) to delete in the fork.

stop.description: Process names and systemd units to disable in the fork.

deviceId.description: The device that owns this; absent or `local` is this device.

force.description: Build again even when the cache holds this spec.

name.description: The recipe's name: a stored recipe (`linux-dev` is always there).

spec.description: Build this spec instead of the stored recipe's.

built.description: False when the cache already held this spec on this image.

files.description: Settings files merged into the computer from forks. Merging appends to it.

keep.description: Run when changes are merged into a computer built from this recipe.

quiet.description: Process names and units stopped in a fork of a computer built from this recipe.

scrub.description: Absolute paths removed from such a fork.

test.description: The command that tests the project; a note for people and agents, never run by Silo.

RecipeDocument.description: A stored recipe with what the engine knows about it.

built.description: The build forks start from, when one exists for this exact spec.

builtIn.description:
Shipped with Silo (`linux-dev`) and not saved by anyone. Saving a recipe with this
name replaces it until that recipe is removed.

hash.description: Content hash of the normalized spec on the current image.

warnings.description:
Things worth knowing about the recipe, such as a quiet service whose process name
cannot be derived.

hash.description: Content hash of the normalized spec.

imageVersion.description: The guest image version it was built on (`unknown` when none is pinned).

deviceId.description: The device that owns this; absent or `local` is this device.

source's record.

computers already built from it keep the text they were built from.

RecipeSpec.description: Everything that decides what a built recipe contains.

desktop.description:
`false`: the computer, and every fork of it, starts no desktop (a Linux recipe;
absent or `true` keeps the desktop on).

setup.description: Commands run once, as root on Linux and as the account on macOS.

RecipeSummary.description: One line of the recipe list.

built.description: A build of this exact spec exists.

saved.description: Every stored recipe, built or not.

forkState.description: `running`, `stopped`, and so on; `None` when the fork no longer exists.

targetName.description: The target computer's name; `None` for a folder or a computer that is gone.

present only for methods that use change admission semantics.

deviceId.description: The device that owns this; absent or `local` is this device.

Less than twice the floor is free: starting another computer works but may slow the device.
Less than the floor is free: an agent inside a computer cannot start or create another.

account.description: The GitHub account a `github-token` secret belongs to, once GitHub confirmed it.

computerIds.description: For a `github-token` secret, the computers whose GitHub access uses it.

kind.description:
`generic` secrets reach a computer as a placeholder for the hosts they allow;
`github-token` secrets reach it only as its GitHub access. Absent on older engines.
A `github-token` secret takes no computers and no hosts here.

SettingsValues.description:
Known settings exposed by 60 §2.3. Unknown keys are rejected by the API;
disk migration and legacy preservation remain engine concerns.

agent.description: The agent the person uses; computers made later suggest it. `null` until chosen.

diskFloorGib.description:
Free disk, in GiB, an agent inside a computer cannot start or create a computer below;
`null` returns to the default (the larger of 10 GiB and 5 % of the disk).

memoryFloorGib.description:
Memory, in GiB, an agent inside a computer cannot start or create a computer below;
`null` returns to the default (the larger of 4 GiB and 10 % of the device's memory).

command.description: The command, joined and cut to 200 characters.

parentCheckpoint.description: For a fork's first step: the checkpoint the fork was made from.

deviceId.description: The device that owns this; absent or `local` is this device.
